answer: I'd like to talk about the most expensive thing I've ever bought for myself. Something expensive I bought after much deliberation was a good-quality laptop for my work and studies. It was a significant purchase for me, so I did not take the decision lightly. I needed it because my old one was painfully slow, and in my job at an education consultancy I'm constantly preparing documents and applications for students. I also wanted something reliable for the online courses I take in the evenings, since I'm hoping to study abroad myself one day. I researched extensively for weeks, comparing models to make sure I was making a [[sensible]] choice. I had saved for it gradually, which made me appreciate its value even more. I [[put aside]] a portion of my salary every month for almost a year, and in the end I paid for it in full, because I didn't want to be paying it off in instalments. When I finally bought it, I felt a mixture of excitement and slight [[apprehension]] at spending so much. However, it quickly proved to be a genuinely [[worthwhile]] investment, as I use it every single day. Its speed and reliability have made my work far more productive. Honestly, although the price was high, the value it has provided over the years has been [[immense]]. It taught me that spending more on something you use constantly is often smarter than buying a cheaper version that disappoints. I have never once regretted the purchase, and I think it was one of my wiser financial decisions.

followUps.q: Have you bought anything expensive since then?
followUps.answer: Nothing on that scale. I tend to be quite careful with money, and I'd rather save towards bigger goals, such as studying abroad, than make [[impulse purchases]] that I might regret later.

followUps.q: Do you prefer to save up or to buy things on credit?
followUps.answer: I definitely prefer to save up first. My father ran his business for over thirty years without borrowing more than he needed, and I suppose I've inherited that cautious attitude.

note: Added why he needed it (consultancy work, study-abroad plans) and how he paid (monthly savings, paid in full); new mark 'put aside'.
